subject: Transfer resilience & DPA annex execution - FinTrust
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@fintrust.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@fintrust.com>, Sara Mendelson <sara.mendelson@fintrust.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Mar 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Transfer resilience questions + DPA annex next steps

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at FinTrust liked the performance profile. Procurement and legal have a couple of follow-ups before we can progress the SOW: a concise matrix showing how Redwood ensures continuity of cross-border processing (fallback routing, model variant failover, and KV-cache recovery), and a completed DPA annex with implementation notes we can share with our internal auditors.

I've attached an XLSX with specific questions mapped to our control families. Can you confirm who will own providing the annex draft vs. technical evidence, and an estimated timeline for delivery?

Cheers,
Liam

Attachments: FinTrust_Data_Transfers_QA.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@fintrust.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Mar 2028 14:33:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Transfer resilience questions + DPA annex next steps

Hi Liam — really appreciate the clear ask and the spreadsheet.

Short answer: Redwood will deliver both (1) a populated DPA annex draft that aligns with your template, and (2) a technical evidence bundle that maps our controls to the questions in your workbook. Proposed owners: Kimberly will take lead on the DPA annex language and commercial clauses; Ben will assemble the technical evidence (logs, routing diagrams, KV-cache behavior, failover runbooks). I will coordinate and sign off.

Timeline: we can deliver a redline-ready DPA annex and the evidence bundle by Wed, 2028-03-21 if we get a small set of clarifications on a few items in your spreadsheet (see inline). Otherwise two options: (A) 2028-03-21 for both deliverables; (B) split deliverables — annex by 2028-03-21, evidence bundle by 2028-03-28. Which would you prefer?

Action: Kimberly and Ben, please see the spreadsheet Liam sent and add a short note in the same sheet on owner / whether we can provide evidence to the exact control or propose an equivalent. I will prepare a draft annex (DPA_Annex_Draft_v2.docx) and circulate for internal review.

— Vivek

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Mar 2028 10:05:00 +0000
Subject: Internal: DPA annex mapping & legal notes

Vivek / Ben — quick status update from legal side after a first pass:

- I reviewed the FinTrust control workbook and flagged three items that will need commercial language (data residency commitments, export exception routing, and audit access windows). I put proposed wording in column G of the sheet.
- On our side the private deployment option + VPC control gives us levers for residency, but procurement asked for fallback guarantees for cross-border sessions — we should be careful with hard SLAs here.
- Suggestion: provide a DPA annex with conditional language that describes fallback model variant routing and an operational escalation path instead of a hard multi-region SLA.

Ben — can you collect the following evidence items and drop into the shared folder by EOD Tue (14 Mar): routing diagram (PDF), KV-cache recovery log example (anonymized), short runbook (markdown) showing canary fallback flow. We will redact any customer-specific IDs.

I'll draft the annex opening clause and attach mapping notes. Vivek, if you agree, I'll circulate the DPA_Annex_Draft_v2.docx to FinTrust with traceability table.

Thanks,
Kimberly

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Mar 2028 16:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Internal: DPA annex mapping & legal notes

Kim / Vivek — uploading engineering artifacts now. Folder link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/FT-2028-0427/evidence

Deliverables attached: routing_diagram_failover.pdf (diagram), kvcache_recovery_example.log (anonymized text), canary_fallback_runbook.md. Short notes: the KV-cache recovery example is taken from a synthetic test run; it shows cache snapshotting and replay within 30s on our Dedicated pool. Canary fallback flow triggers when 5XX per-minute crosses threshold X; automatic reroute to model-variant with degraded throughput but matched safety config.

I recommend we avoid exact numeric SLAs in the annex; instead reference our operational playbook and offer a canary-based validated DR test schedule (quarterly).

— Ben

Attachments: routing_diagram_failover.pdf (diagram, 180KB); kvcache_recovery_example.log (txt, 12KB); canary_fallback_runbook.md (text, 8KB)
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@fintrust.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@fintrust.com>, Sara Mendelson <sara.mendelson@fintrust.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Mar 2028 17:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Transfer resilience questions + DPA annex next steps

Thanks all — that plan sounds workable. Procurement prefers Option A (both annex + evidence by 21 Mar) if Redwood can keep the annex language that provides operational guarantees + a quarterly validated DR test, rather than a hard SLA. Legal will review your redline but asked a small set of clarifying questions (see below).

Clarifications needed:
1) In the annex we need a short sentence describing the geographic routing hierarchy and which regions are considered 'fallback' for EU-hosted sessions.
2) For the DR test cadence, can you confirm whether Redwood will provide a post-test attestation (signed by an engineer) and a summary report (pass/fail + deviations)?
3) For audit access, FinTrust needs a 30-day window for on-demand access to request logs for specific sessions — is that operationally feasible without prior notice?

If you can confirm #1-#3 in writing we will queue legal review and aim to issue a PO to get this started.

Thanks — Liam

On Wed, Mar 14, 2028 at 16:22, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com> wrote:
> Kim / Vivek — uploading engineering artifacts now....
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@fintrust.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@fintrust.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Mar 2028 18:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Transfer resilience questions + DPA annex next steps

Liam — quick consolidated responses for your legal team (we will include these in the annex and evidence bundle):

1) Geographic routing hierarchy: Primary EU region = eu-west-1 (customer-tagged sessions); Fallback regions = eu-central-1 then us-west-2 (only if eu capacity constrained). We'll add the explicit sentence you requested and also a short diagram in the annex.

2) DR test cadence attestation: Redwood will run quarterly validated DR tests against live-like synthetic workloads and provide a post-test attestation signed by the engineering lead plus a one-page summary report (pass/fail + deviation notes). We'll include a template attestation in the evidence bundle.

3) Audit access window: We can provide on-demand access to session-level logs within a 30-day window subject to a formal audit request (data minimization and redaction rules apply). For extremely time-sensitive incidents we recommend a dedicated audit-support agreement (add-on) to guarantee sub-48h turnaround; otherwise standard is 72 hours to deliver requested artifacts after a qualified request.

Next steps: Kimberly will issue the annex redline by Mon 2028-03-20 EOD; Ben will finalize the evidence bundle and upload the attestation template. If procurement confirms Option A we will treat this as priority and attach the draft to the HubSpot deal record.

— Vivek
